BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.claim: He links this surah to earlier warnings about human ignorance and injustice and cites the ungrateful person, humanity in loss, and the man who thinks wealth makes him immortal.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تضمنت السور المتقدمة من الوعيد لمن انطوى على ما ذكر فيها

BURSEVI:v10p392/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p392/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p392/r1.claim: Inwardly, the collected wealth is a hoard of blameworthy morals and low qualities, treated as provision for the stages of the afterlife and entry into God’s presence.
BURSEVI:v10p392/r1.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية جمع مال الأخلاق الذميمة والأوصاف الرديئة وجعله عدة منازل الآخرة والدخول على الله

BURSEVI:v10p392/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p392/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p392/r2.claim: The person behaves as though wealth will immortalize him, building sturdy structures, planting trees, and digging rivers; the belief is figurative, not an actual conviction.
BURSEVI:v10p392/r2.anchor: أي يعمل من تشييد البنيان وإيثاقه بالصخر والآجر وغرس الأشجار

BURSEVI:v10p392/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p392/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
BURSEVI:v10p392/r3.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says the miser thinks his money will convey him to an immortal station; the past tense depicts wealth as having already guaranteed survival and safety from death.
BURSEVI:v10p392/r3.anchor: يظن أنه ماله يوصله إلى مقام الخلد وإنما قال أخلده

BURSEVI:v10p392/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p392/r4.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v10p392/r4.claim: Al-Hasan observes that death is certain, yet resembles a matter doubted by people who lack certainty.
BURSEVI:v10p392/r4.anchor: ما رأيت يقينا لا شك فيه أشبه بشك لا يقين فيه كالموت

BURSEVI:v10p392/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p392/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p392/r5.claim: Kalla rebukes the false belief that wealth makes a person immortal; it may also rebuke the earlier mockery and answer an implied oath that the person will certainly be cast down.
BURSEVI:v10p392/r5.anchor: ردع له عن ذلك الحسبان الباطل يعني نه نانست كه آدمى ندارد

BURSEVI:v10p392/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p392/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p392/r6.claim: Another grammatical reading refers the dual verb to both the hamza and the lamza, supported by a recitation that uses the dual form.
BURSEVI:v10p392/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم ولك أن ترد الضمير إلى كل من الهمزة واللمزة ويؤيده قراءة لينبذان على التثنية

QASHANI:104:1-3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:104:1-3/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:104:1-3/r3.claim: Wealth cannot immortalize its owner; lasting knowledge and spiritual virtues can, while bodily riches perish and long hopes conceal sudden death.
QASHANI:104:1-3/r3.anchor: أي: لا يشعر أن المقتنيات المخلدة لصاحبها هي العلوم والفضائل النفسانية الباقية

QASHANI:104:1-3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:104:1-3/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:104:1-3/r4.claim: Ignorance, a vice of the royal faculty, is the root of all vices; the immersed deserve eternal punishment that overwhelms the heart and destroys its substance.
QASHANI:104:1-3/r4.anchor: والحاصل أن الجهل الذي هو رذيلة القوة الملكية أصل جميع الرذائل ومستلزم لها

QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r7.claim: The miser imagines that his wealth will keep him alive in this world.
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r7.anchor: { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } . أي : يبقيه في الدنيا

SULAMI:v2p420#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p420#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p420#2/r1.claim: He thinks his wealth will bring him to the station of eternal life.
SULAMI:v2p420#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : يظن أن ماله يوصله إلى مقام الخلد

TUSTARI:104:3/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:104:3/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:104:3/r1.claim: He thinks his wealth will make him immortal in the abode of permanence.

TUSTARI:104:3/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:104:3/r2.speaker: قيل
TUSTARI:104:3/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that he thinks wealth will protect him from death.

AKHFASH:v2p584/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p584/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p584/r2.claim: يحسب أن ماله أخلده كلا لينبذن means that he and his wealth will be cast into the Crusher.
AKHFASH:v2p584/r2.anchor: [وقال] {يحسب أن ماله أخلده} {كلا لينبذن في الحطمة} أي: هو وماله.

FARRA:v3p289#2/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p289#2/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p289#2/r5.claim: أخلده means “will make him live forever”; the past form can express a future result, as when one says a sinner entered Hell meaning Hell is due for him.
FARRA:v3p289#2/r5.anchor: يحسب أن ماله أخلده (3) يريد: يخلده

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3463#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3463#3/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3463#3/r1.claim: Ikrima interprets the belief that wealth made its owner immortal as the belief that it would extend his lifespan.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3463#3/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة قوله : يحسب ان ماله اخلده قال : يزيد في عمره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r6.claim: The claim that wealth immortalizes its owner may be a sarcastic circumstantial portrait of the hoarder, a detached assertion of denial, or a taunting rhetorical question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r6.anchor: وجملة : { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } يجوز أن تكون حالا من همزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r7.claim: Past akhlada treats the future as already accomplished because the hoarder is so certain that money has granted immortality, intensifying the satire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r7.anchor: وجيء بصيغة المضي في { أخلده } لتنزيل المستقبل منزلة الماضي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r1.claim: The hamza in akhlada is causative: wealth supposedly makes its possessor immortal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r1.anchor: والهمزة في { أخلده } للتعدية ، أي جعله خالدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r2.claim: Most readers pronounce yaḥsabu with kasra on the sīn; Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and Abū Jaʿfar use fatḥa, two dialectal forms.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r3.claim: The hoarder behaves as if wealth could ward off death and grant the worldly immortality that is his greatest wish, since he denies another eternal life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r3.anchor: أن المال يقيهم الموت ويجعلهم خالدين لأن الخلود في الدنيا أقصى متمناهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r4.claim: Kallā refutes the idea that wealth immortalizes and rebukes obsessive hoarding that prevents paying God's due through spending and zakāt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p539/r4.anchor: وزجر عن التلبس بالحالة الشنيعة التي جعلتهم في حال من يحسب أن المال يخلد صاحبه

NAHHAS:v5p287/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p287/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p287/r11.claim: The kasra reading of يحسب is described as the Prophet’s dialect, on the rare pattern فعِل يفعَل.
NAHHAS:v5p287/r11.anchor: يقال هي لغة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بكسر السين جاء على فعل يفعل وله نظائر يسيرة

NAHHAS:v5p287/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p287/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p287/r12.claim: The أن clause and its governed words occupy the two objects of يحسب.
NAHHAS:v5p287/r12.anchor: أن وما عملت فيه في موضع المفعولين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r2.claim: The miser thinks wealth is the substance and support of his life: it preserved him so far and, he imagines, will preserve him forever.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r2.anchor: وقوله: يحسب أن ماله أخلده معناه: يحسب أن ماله هو معنى حياته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r4.speaker: الأعرج وأبو جعفر وشيبة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r4.claim: They read يَحْسَب with fatḥa on س.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ: «يحسب» بفتح السين الأعرج وأبو جعفر وشيبة،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p229/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p229/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p229/r1.claim: “Made him immortal” means “will make him immortal”: the person thinks wealth will protect him from death and acts as if he will not die.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p229/r1.anchor: أخلده بمعنى يخلده والمعنى يظن ماله مانعا له من الموت فهو يعمل عمل من لا يظن أنه يموت

IBNKATHIR:104:3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:104:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:104:3/r1.claim: He supposes that collecting wealth will make him immortal in this world.
IBNKATHIR:104:3/r1.anchor: أي : يظن أن جمعه المال يخلده في هذه الدار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r16.claim: Akhledahu and khalladahu both mean that wealth lengthened his hopes until he imagined it would keep him alive forever.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r16.anchor: أخلده } وخلده بمعنى أي : طول المال أمله ، ومناه الأماني البعيدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r17.claim: Alternatively, he builds fortified homes, plants trees, and develops the land as though wealth made him live forever.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r17.anchor: أو يعمل من تشييد البنيان الموثق بالصخر والآجر وغرس الأشجار وعمارة الأرض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r18.claim: A further interpretation makes the wording an ironic allusion to good works, which truly make their doer abide in bliss; wealth does not.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r18.anchor: أو هو تعريض بالعمل الصالح . وأنه هو الذي أخلد صاحبه في النعيم ؛ فأما المال فما أخلد أحدا فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r19.claim: Reports say al-Akhnas had either four thousand or ten thousand dinars.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r19.anchor: وروي أنه كان للأخنس أربعة آلاف دينار . وقيل : عشرة آلاف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r21.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r21.claim: Kalla rebukes the man's belief that wealth made him immortal.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r14.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r14.claim: He thinks his wealth will lengthen his life.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r15.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r15.claim: He thinks his wealth will prevent death.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r16.claim: A further possibility is that he thinks his wealth will benefit him after death.

MUQATIL:104:1-9/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r5.claim: He imagines his wealth will preserve him from death until the wealth itself is spent.
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r5.anchor: من الموت، فلا يموت حتى يفنى ماله

MUQATIL:104:1-9/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r6.claim: God rejects this belief: neither his wealth nor his children will make him immortal.
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r6.anchor: يقول الله عز وجل { كلا } لا يخلده ماله وولده

MUQATIL:104:1-5/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r2.claim: The narrative says the man swore he could distribute his wealth throughout Quraysh while alive without exhausting it, and challenged the threat of poverty.
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r2.anchor: قسم مالى يمينا وشمالا على قريش ما دمت حيا ما فنى، فكيف تعدنى الفقر

MUQATIL:104:1-5/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r3.claim: He is told that the One who gave him his wealth can take it away; this affects him, and he begins counting his possessions.
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r3.anchor: إن الذي أعطاك، قادر على أن يأخذه منك، فوقع في قلبه من ذلك شىء، ثم عمد إلى ماله فعده

MUQATIL:104:1-5/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r5.claim: He tells Muhammad that even if all his counted wealth were bread it would not run out, and the condemnation in Sūrat al-Humazah is revealed in response.
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r5.anchor: يا محمد تعدنى الفقر والله لو كان هذا خبزا ما فنى، فأنزل الله عز وجل

MUQATIL:104:1-5/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r6.claim: He repeats that the man's wealth will not make him immortal.
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r6.anchor: كلا } لا يخلده، ثم استأنف، فقال: { لينبذن في الحطمة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#3/r1.claim: He thinks his wealth will make him immortal in this world, so that he will not die.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#3/r1.anchor: أى تركه خالدا فى الدنيا لا يموت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, the phrase alludes to righteous deeds as what grant lasting bliss; wealth has made no one immortal.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#3/r2.anchor: أو هو تعريض بالعمل الصالح وأنه هو الذى أخلده صاحبه فى النعيم فأما المال فما أخلد أحدا فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r1.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the miser imagines wealth will keep him alive forever.
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { يحسب } أي يظن { أن ماله أخلده } أي يبقيه حيا لا يموت قاله السدي.

QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r2.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r2.claim: ʿIkrimah says he imagines his wealth will extend his lifespan.
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r2.anchor: وقال عكرمة: أي يزيد في عمره.

QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r3.claim: Another reading treats the past tense as future, as when Arabic says someone died and entered Hell meaning he will enter it.
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r3.anchor: وقيل: أحياه فيما مضى، وهو ماض بمعنى المستقبل.

QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r4.claim: Kallā refutes the unbeliever's assumption: wealth cannot make him immortal or remain with him.
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r4.anchor: { كلا } رد لما توهمه الكافر أي لا يخلد ولا يبقى له مال.

QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r5.speaker: عمر بن عبد الله مولى غفرة
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r5.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allah, client of Ghufrah, says that when God says kallā, He tells the hearer that he is wrong.
QURTUBI-FULL:104:3-6/r5.anchor: وقال عمر بن عبد الله مولى غفرة: إذا سمعت الله عز وجل يقول «كلا» فإنه يقول كذبت.

QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r1.claim: The wealthy person imagines money can do anything, including warding off death, securing lasting life, and escaping God’s decree and judgment.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r1.anchor: كما يروح يحسب أن هذا المال إله قادر على كل شيء ؛ لا يعجز عن فعل شيء ! حتى دفع الموت وتخليد الحياة

QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r2.claim: Obsessive attachment to wealth leads him to count and savor it while scorning people’s dignity and mocking them through words and gestures.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r2.anchor: ينطلق في هوس بهذا المال يعده ويستلذ تعداده ؛ وتنطلق في كيانه نفخة فاجرة ، تدفعه إلى الاستهانة بأقدار الناس

QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r3.claim: Islam detests and forbids mockery and faultfinding; the sura’s severe warning suggests actual polytheists targeted the Messenger and believers, but Quṭb considers reports identifying particular people unreliable.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r3.anchor: وقد وردت روايات بتعيين بعض الشخصيات . ولكنها ليست وثيقة . فنكتفي نحن بما قررناه عنها

QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r4.claim: The afterlife scene proportionately reverses the crime: the rich scoffer who imagines wealth guarantees permanence is discarded and crushed in al-Ḥuṭama, the uniquely terrifying Fire attributed to God.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r4.anchor: المهمل المتردي في( الحطمة )التي تحطم كل ما يلقى إليها

QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r5.claim: The Fire reaches his heart, source of mockery, arrogance, and pride, then confines him without aid or regard, tied to a pillar like an animal.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r5.anchor: على فؤاده الذي ينبعث منه الهمز واللمز ، وتكمن فيه السخرية والكبرياء والغرور

QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r6.claim: Quṭb notes emphatic sounds and rhetorical progression—threat, ambiguity, an awe-inspiring question, and explanation—to magnify the punishment and harmonize its imagery with the mocker’s acts.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r6.anchor: ثم سؤال الاستهوال . ثم الإجابة والبيان . . كلها من أساليب التوكيد والتضخيم

QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r7.claim: The Qur’an directs the mission while recounting it, destroying enemies’ plots and strengthening believers; God’s answer both condemns ethical degradation and reassures the oppressed that He sees, hates, and punishes their abuse.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:3/r7.anchor: إشعارهم بأن الله يرى ما يقع لهم ، ويكرهه ، ويعاقب عليه

RAZI:104:3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:104:3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:104:3/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī says akhladahu and khalladahu have the same meaning, then records four interpretations of the claim that wealth makes its possessor endure.
RAZI:104:3/r1.anchor: واعلم أن أخلده وخلده بمعنى واحد ثم في التفسير وجوه

RAZI:104:3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:104:3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:104:3/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan’s interpretation is that wealth lengthens the person’s hopes until, through heedlessness, he thinks it has made him immortal; the past tense pictures immortality as an already-secured guarantee against death.
RAZI:104:3/r2.anchor: قال الحسن : ما رأيت يقينا لا شك فيه أشبه بشك لا يقين فيه كالموت

RAZI:104:3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:104:3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:104:3/r3.claim: A second interpretation is that he constructs durable buildings of brick and plaster as someone expecting to live on or to be remembered after death.
RAZI:104:3/r3.anchor: يعمل الأعمال المحكمة كتشييد البنيان بالآجر والجص

RAZI:104:3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:104:3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:104:3/r4.claim: A third view says he loves wealth so intensely that he imagines losing any of it would kill him and preserves it to stay alive; al-Rāzī considers this plausible for a miser.
RAZI:104:3/r4.anchor: أحب المال حبا شديدا حتى اعتقد أنه إن انتقص مالي أموت

RAZI:104:3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:104:3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:104:3/r5.claim: A fourth interpretation treats the statement as an allusion to righteous deeds, which preserve their doer through good remembrance in this world and enduring bliss in the next.
RAZI:104:3/r5.anchor: أن هذا تعريض بالعمل الصالح وأنه هو الذي يخلد صاحبه في الدنيا بالذكر الجميل

RAZI:104:3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:104:3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:104:3/r6.claim: One reading of kalla rebukes the delusion: wealth does not make one immortal, whereas knowledge and righteousness endure; ʿAlī is quoted saying wealth keepers die while scholars remain through time.
RAZI:104:3/r6.anchor: ومنه قول علي عليه السلام : مات خزان المال وهم أحياء والعلماء باقون ما بقي الدهر

RAZI:104:3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:104:3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:104:3/r7.claim: The second reading takes kalla to mean “indeed”; the lām in layunbadhanna answers an implied oath, conveying the force of an oath in kalla.
RAZI:104:3/r7.anchor: والقول الثاني معناه حقا : { لينبذن } واللام في : { لينبذن } جواب القسم المقدر

STUDYQURAN:104:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:104:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:104:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah focuses on the torment awaiting people who spend worldly life hoarding wealth.
STUDYQURAN:104:intro/r6.anchor: focus upon the torment that awaits one who spends the life of this world hoarding wealth

STUDYQURAN:104:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:104:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:104:2/r1.claim: The hoarder's punishment is vividly described in 9:34–35: hoarded gold and silver brand their owners in Hell.
STUDYQURAN:104:2/r1.anchor: The punishment for those who hoard is most vividly described in 9:34–35

SAMIN-DURR:104:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:104:3/r1.claim: يحسب may begin an independent sentence or function as a circumstantial clause describing the subject of جمع.
SAMIN-DURR:104:3/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون مستأنفة، وأن تكون حالا من فاعل " جمع "

SAMIN-DURR:104:3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:104:3/r2.claim: أخلده may mean يخلده, with a past form used for the present; alternatively it retains its past sense, meaning the wealth prolonged his life.
SAMIN-DURR:104:3/r2.anchor: و " أخلده " يعني يخلده، فأوقع الماضي موقع المضارع. وقيل: هو على أصله، أي: أطال عمره

TAB-FULL:v24p621/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p621/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p621/r1.claim: The miser thinks his amassed wealth will keep him alive and remove death; al-Ṭabarī explains the past form as a future consequence, as when an act is said to have destroyed someone before its result occurs.
TAB-FULL:v24p621/r1.anchor: يعطب من فعله ذلك، ولما يهلك بعد ولم يعطب؛ وكالرجل يأتي الموبقة من الذنوب: دخل والله فلان النار

ZAJJAJ:v5p362/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p362/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p362/r1.claim: He acts like a wealthy person who does not think that he will die, as if his wealth made him immortal.
ZAJJAJ:v5p362/r1.anchor: أي يعمل عمل من لا يظن مع يساره أنه يموت

TABATABAI:104:1-3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r8.claim: He thinks wealth will preserve him in worldly life and prevent death; the past-tense verb is prospective because of the preceding thinks.
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r8.anchor: أي يخلده في الدنيا ويدفع عنه الموت والفناء فالماضي أريد به المستقبل بقرينة قوله

TABATABAI:104:1-3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r9.claim: Attachment to earth and endless hope make him crave more than life's brief needs; he mistakes wealth for immortality, and the accumulation and perceived self-sufficiency produce tyranny and superiority over others.
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r9.anchor: زاد مالا زاد حرصا إلى ما لا نهاية له فظاهر حاله أنه يرى أن المال يخلده، ولحبه الغريزي للبقاء يهتم

TABATABAI:104:3-6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:104:3-6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:104:3-6/r1.claim: Feeling self-sufficient makes a person rebel; the arrogance born of wealth's perceived sufficiency leads to fault-finding and mockery, and the causal sequence links hoarding to the warning against slander.
TABATABAI:104:3-6/r1.anchor: ويورثه هذا الاستكبار والتعدي الهمز واللمز. ومن هنا يظهر أن قوله

TABATABAI:104:3-6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:104:3-6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:104:3-6/r2.claim: The rebuke rejects the delusion of immortality; the oath-emphasizing lām promises he will die and be cast into the Hutama, the crushing fire of Hell.
TABATABAI:104:3-6/r2.anchor: للقسم، والنبذ القذف والطرح، والحطمة مبالغة من الحطم وهو الكسر

TABATABAI:104:3-6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:104:3-6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:104:3-6/r3.claim: Hutama intensifies crushing and can also mean eating; it is one of Hell's names, explained by the coming phrase God's kindled fire.
TABATABAI:104:3-6/r3.anchor: وجاء بمعنى الأكل، وهي من أسماء جهنم على ما يفسرها قوله الآتي

TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r15.claim: The hoarder thinks wealth will keep him alive and protect him from death; the past verb means the future because “he thinks” governs it, and he acts as though hoping for immortality despite knowing everyone dies.
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r15.anchor: يظن أن ماله الذي جمعه يخلده في الدنيا ويمنعه من الموت

TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r16.claim: Alternatively, “made immortal” means that wealth caused immortality, as when someone is said to have perished once the cause arose even before death occurred.
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r16.anchor: أخلده بمعنى أوجب إخلاده وهذا كما يقال هلك فلان

THALABI:v10p286/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p286/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p286/r10.claim: The claim that wealth made its owner immortal in this world is refuted by كلا.
THALABI:v10p286/r10.anchor: يحسب أن ماله أخلده في الدنيا كلا رد عليه

THALABI:v10p286/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p286/r11.speaker: عمر بن عبد الله مولى غفرة
THALABI:v10p286/r11.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh, the client of Ghufra, says that whenever God says كلا, He is declaring the claim false.
THALABI:v10p286/r11.anchor: يقول: إذا سمعت الله سبحانه يقول: كلا فإنما يقول: كذبت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq says he acts as though his wealth will keep him from dying.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r5.anchor: أي يعمل عمل من لا يظن مع يساره أنه يموت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r6.claim: His wealth cannot make him immortal or remain with him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r6.anchor: كلا} لا يخلده (ماله) (¬10)، ولا يبقى له

WAHIDI-QT:104:3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:104:3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:104:3/r1.claim: He thinks his wealth has made him immortal in this world, so that he will not die.

ASAD-NOTES:104:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1/r1.claim: The surah condemns slander and fault-finding alongside amassing wealth and treating it as protection that will secure immortality.
ASAD-NOTES:104:1/r1.anchor: WOE unto every slanderer, fault-finder! [1] (104:2) [Woe unto him[2]] who amasses wealth and counts it a safeguard

ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n2/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n2/r1.claim: Asad inserts the repeated “Woe unto him” because verses 2–3 describe a blameworthy attitude distinct from the two types in verse 1.
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n2/r1.anchor: This repetitive interpolation is necessary because the blameworthy attitude spoken of in verses 2-3 obviously belongs to a category entirely different

ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n3/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n3/r1.claim: Counting wealth as a safeguard is a metonym for treating material acquisition as almost religious, displacing spiritual concerns.
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n3/r1.anchor: a metonym for the tendency to attribute an almost "religious" value to the acquisition and possession of material goods

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r1.claim: Woe formulas followed by vice catalogues also occur at 107:4–7, 83:1–3, 83:10–11, 52:11–12, and 51:60; 83:1–6 is especially close in its wealth theme and following rhetorical question.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Durch wail eingeleitete Wehsprüche mit folgendem Lasterkatalog finden sich sonst noch in 107:4–7, 83:1–3, 83:10.11 und 52:11.12

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r2.claim: Woe speeches as a basic form of prophetic discourse already appear in the Hebrew Bible, for example Micah 2:1–3.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Wehsprüche als grundlegende Form prophetischer Rede begegnen bereits in der Hebräischen Bibel

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:3:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:3:anmerkung/r1.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:3:anmerkung/r1.claim: Neuwirth once proposed adding the question particle to yahsabu because the other four early Meccan uses have it and 83:1–6 offers a parallel woe followed by a polemical question; she later seems to withdraw the emendation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:3:anmerkung/r1.anchor: hat Neuwirth dafür argumentiert, yaḥsabu in 104:4 zu ʾa-yaḥsabu zu emendieren (Neuwirth, Studien, 233 f.). In ihrer jüngsten Veröffentlichung scheint sie jedoch

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:3:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:3:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:3:anmerkung/r2.claim: The pursuit of immortality, khuld, is a motif of pre-Islamic poetry; Neuwirth cites Tarafa's Muallaqa verse 54 as evidence.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:3:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Das Streben nach „Ewigkeit“ bzw. „Unsterblichkeit“ (ḫuld) ist ein Motiv der altarabischen Dichtung

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r1.claim: The opening woe, vice list, and insult sketch a prototypical sinner who trusts without basis that money grants immortality, driving antisocial conduct and limitless accumulation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r1.anchor: Der einleitende Wehspruch mit Lasterkatalog (V. 1.2) sowie das anschließende Scheltwort entwerfen das Charakterporträt eines prototypischen Sünders.

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r2.claim: This hoarding is the opposite of ostentatious spending criticized at 90:6, yet both reflect the delusion that people can secure immortality by their own power.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r2.anchor: Das kritisierte Verhalten bildet damit das genaue Gegenteil der in 90:6 angeprangerten ostentativen Besitzverschwendung

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r3.claim: Verse 4 counters the imagined immortality with punishment: instead of living forever, the sinner is shattered in Hell, expressed by the root h-t-m.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r3.anchor: Das Handeln des Getadelten hat gerade nicht seine Unsterblichkeit zur Folge, sondern zieht im Gegenteil seine „Zertrümmerung“ (ḥ-ṭ-m) in der Hölle nach sich.

ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r14.claim: The miser imagines wealth has already made him immortal, trusts it to save him from every danger, and builds all hopes on it.

ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r15.claim: Elmalılı rejects that presumption: lasting life comes through faith in truth, knowledge, and righteous action, as the preceding surah explained.
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r15.anchor: üzere Hakk’a iman ve ilim ile amel-i sâlihtir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r1.claim: The hypocrites think wealth will buy them eternal life, and their total absorption in it shows they seek every pleasure through wealth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r1.anchor: wealth will also buy for them eternal life.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r2.claim: If they recognized that wealth and life are temporary, they would spend for the Hereafter and compete in doing so.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r2.anchor: If they knew that both their wealth and life were

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r3.claim: Al-Shu‘ara depicts the same false permanence in people building monuments and palaces as though they would live forever.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r3.anchor: build grand palaces as if you have to live here forever?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r4.claim: A person’s attitude, rather than stated beliefs, reveals the inner self; life differs according to whether this world or the next is the final destination.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r4.anchor: attitude towards life and not what he says

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r5.speaker: Jesus (sws)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r5.claim: Jesus teaches that people should keep their wealth with God, because the heart follows wherever wealth is; Islahi uses this to explain why afterlife belief precludes hoarding.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p449/r5.anchor: Keep your wealth with God, because your heart is wherever your wealth is.

QIRAAT-ER:104:3:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:104:3:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:104:3:1#1/r1.claim: Yaḥsibu with kasra on sīn is a canonical variant of yaḥsabu with fatḥa; both mean he supposes and differ only in vocal pattern.
QIRAAT-ER:104:3:1#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with kasra on the sin (yaḥsibu vs yaḥsabu). Both are mutawatir readings

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r2.claim: The surah is Meccan and explains the loser mentioned at the end of the previous surah by describing a particular kind of loser.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r2.anchor: هذه السورة مكية. لما قال فيما قبلها: إن الإنسان لفي خسر ، بين حال الخاسر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r1.claim: The sentence is either circumstantial or a fresh sentence; akhladahu and khalladahu both mean that wealth left him everlasting, either without end or for an extremely long time.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r1.anchor: جملة حالية أو استئنافية وأخلده وخلده بمعنى أى تركه خالدا أى ماكثا لايتناهى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r2.claim: The phrase is a representational metaphor: wealth lengthens his hopes, so he builds, plants, and digs as though he thought it would keep him alive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r2.anchor: والكلام من باب الاستعارة التمثيلية والمراد ان المال طول أمله ومناه الاماني البعيدة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r3.claim: Naming wealth explicitly where a pronoun could stand increases emphasis, and the past tense intensifies the intended meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r3.anchor: والاظهار في مقام الاضمار لزيادة التقرير والتعبير بالماضي للمبالغة في المعنى المراد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r4.claim: He may literally think wealth made him immortal because delusion and preoccupation with accumulation distract him from the terrors ahead, or because he believes life and safety depend on outward causes and wealth governs them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يراد انه حاسب ذلك حقيقة لفرط غروره واشتغاله بالجمع والتكاثر عما امامه من قوارع الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r5.claim: Another reading says he counts wealth among the things that grant immortality, hinting that the truly worthy pursuit is the afterlife; Alusi calls this very far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد انه يحسب المال من المخلدات ولانظر فيه إلى ان الخلود دنيوي أو اخروى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r6.claim: Alusi says the afterlife allusion is too far-fetched, and notes that a distinguished scholar did not treat it as an independent interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r6.anchor: والغرض منه التعريض بان ثم مخلدا ينبغي للعاقل أن يكب عليه وهو السعى للآخرة وهو بعيد جدا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r7.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r7.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn proposes that the subject of ‘made immortal’ is the hoarder and its object is wealth: he thinks he can preserve it forever, unaware that mishap or death will take it; Alusi rejects the proposal.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r8.claim: A saying warns that a miser’s wealth should expect a mishap or an heir, illustrating that he cannot keep it forever.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230#2/r8.anchor: كما قيل بشر مال البخيل بحادث أو وارث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r3.claim: He thinks his wealth has made him immortal in this life and that his prosperity means he will not die.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r3.anchor: {يحسب أن ماله أخلده} في الدنيا، يظن أنه لا يموت مع يساره.

BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r6.claim: The man may think wealth left him immortal, be distracted from death by loving it, or develop such long hopes that he lives as if he will not die.
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r6.anchor: تركه خالدا في الدنيا فأحبه كما يحب الخلود، أو حب المال أغفله عن الموت

BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r7.claim: The wording hints that true immortality lies in striving for the afterlife.

BINTSHATI:v2p172/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r3.claim: Ḥisāb means counting materially and estimation, planning, or accountability figuratively; religious reckoning is especially associated with God.
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r3.anchor: كما تستعمله معنوياً في التقدير والتدبير

BINTSHATI:v2p172/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r4.claim: Arabic commonly uses kasra for counting and fatḥa for estimation; ḥasab also means inherited family distinctions.
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r4.anchor: فيغلب كسر السين للحساب بمعنى العد

BINTSHATI:v2p172/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r5.claim: Qur'anic tri-form hasiba occurs with the sense of estimation by supposition, as when the Queen of Sheba mistakes the floor for water.
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r5.anchor: يؤذن سياقها أنها بمعنى التقدير عن ظن

BINTSHATI:v2p173/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r1.claim: Interrogative uses of hasiba often rebuke deluded assumptions about escaping trial, equaling believers, hidden grudges, or purposeless creation.
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r1.anchor: ويكثر مجيئه بأسلوب الاستفهام الإنكاري، فيعطيه السياق دلالة ضلال الوهم

BINTSHATI:v2p173/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r2.claim: All thirty-one occurrences of the open-fātha present yaḥsabu warn against human misestimation.
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r2.anchor: بمجئ الفعل المضارع مفتوح السين في آياته الإحدى والثلاثين

BINTSHATI:v2p173/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r3.claim: Thus the word in al-Humazah means a false assumption that wealth made its owner immortal.
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r3.anchor: على التوهم الذي يخطئ حقيقة التقدير

BINTSHATI:v2p173/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r4.claim: Khuld means permanent endurance; the Qur'an reserves eternal life for the afterlife and denies worldly immortality for human beings.
BINTSHATI:v2p173/r4.anchor: والخلد في العربية البقاء والدوام، استعملته حسياً

BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r2.claim: Because of foolishness, he thinks his counted wealth makes him immortal in this world; alternatively, his immersion in sin and pleasure shows he acts as though he will never die, while only righteous deeds secure eternal life in the Hereafter.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك كناية عن أنه عمل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r3.claim: Kallā rejects the fantasy: he will die like every other created living being.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r3.anchor: بل يموت كما مات كل حي مخلوق

DURR:104:3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:104:3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:104:3/r1.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports that the Prophet recited yaḥsabu with kasrah on the sīn; Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Ḥākim authenticated this report, also cited by Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khaṭīb.
DURR:104:3/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } بكسر السين

DURR:104:3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:104:3/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:104:3/r2.claim: ʿIkrimah explains the claim that wealth made him immortal as meaning it increases his lifespan.
DURR:104:3/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } قال : يزيد في عمره

RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r1.claim: Akhladahu and khalladahu have the same meaning.

RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r2.claim: One interpretation is that wealth prolongs a person's hopes until he imagines it has made him immortal; the past tense portrays survival as a guarantee already settled.
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r2.anchor: يحسب هذا الإنسان أن المال ضمن له الخلود وأعطاه الأمان من الموت

RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r3.claim: Hasan remarks that death is the certain reality most like a doubt to which people give no credence.
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r3.anchor: قال الحسن : ما رأيت يقينا لا شك فيه أشبه بشك لا يقين فيه كالموت

RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r4.claim: A second interpretation is that he builds sturdy structures as someone expecting a long life or hoping to be remembered after death.
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r4.anchor: يعمل الأعمال المحكمة كتشييد البنيان بالآجر والجص

RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r5.claim: A third interpretation is an extreme love of wealth: the miser imagines losing any of it would mean dying, so he hoards to preserve life.
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r5.anchor: ثالثها : أحب المال حبا شديدا حتى اعتقد أنه : إن انتقص مالي أموت

RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r6.claim: A fourth interpretation alludes to righteous deeds, which preserve a person's good name in this world and bring enduring bliss in the next.
RAZI-FULL:v32p88#2/r6.anchor: أن هذا تعريض بالعمل الصالح وأنه هو الذي يخلد صاحبه في الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r4.claim: Akhladahu means the wealth made him seem immortal, since it sustained and protected his life for its duration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r4.anchor: أخلده: أي أبقاه حيا، إذ به قوام حياته وحفظه مدة عمره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says long-lasting wealth extended his hopes until, through heedlessness, he imagined money would keep him alive forever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أي طول المال أمله ومناه الأماني البعيدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r7.claim: Kalla rebukes the man's belief that his wealth will make him immortal.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.claim: Sibawayh groups three conjugation patterns as shared by transitive and intransitive verbs, including faʿala-yafʿilu, faʿila-yafʿalu, and faʿala-yafʿulu.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.anchor: اعلم أنه يكون كل ما تعداك إلى غيرك على ثلاثة أبنية على فعل يفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.claim: Intransitive verbs have a fourth pattern, faʿula-yafʿulu, which transitive verbs do not share; Sibawayh says there is no transitive faʿultuhu.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.anchor: ضرب رابع لا يشركه فيه ما يتعداك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.claim: The fourth pattern marks intransitivity; the other three past-tense patterns and their corresponding imperfect patterns are shared across transitive and intransitive verbs.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.anchor: فضروب الأفعال أربعة يجتمع في ثلاثة ما يتعداك وما

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.claim: Sibawayh lists ḥasiba-yaḥsabu among verbs with a nonstandard imperfect vowel; the fatḥa form is sound and more analogical.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.anchor: وذلك حسب يحسب ويئس ييئس ويبس ييبس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.claim: Sibawayh cites al-Farazdaq’s line to attest the imperfect yanʿamu with ḍamma, describing guests’ delight or comfort.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.claim: A few verbs occur with ḍamma in the imperfect despite their usual pattern; Sibawayh gives faḍila-yafḍulu and māta-tamūtu and notes more analogical forms.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابعلمكلفعلتعداكإلىغيرك)#67.claim: Al-Khalīl calls the reported kāda-takādu pattern irregular, comparing it with the irregular faḍila-yafḍulu class.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.claim: For verbs with initial hamza, such as amara-yaʾmuru and akala-yaʾkulu, Sibawayh explains the imperfect vowel by analogy with assimilation and the treatment of a medial hamza.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.anchor: تقول أمر يأمر وأبق يأبق وأكل يأكل وأفل يأفل لأنها ساكنة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.claim: He also relates the following vowel to how a medial hamza and its counterparts would open a neighboring letter, while avoiding an opening that conflicts with a quiescent initial hamza.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.anchor: الذي قبل اللام فتحته اللام في قرأ يقرأ

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.claim: Sibawayh explains abā-yaʾbā by analogy with qaraʾa-yaqraʾu, while also allowing an analogy with ḥasiba-yaḥsabu.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.anchor: وقالوا أبى يأبى فشبهوه بيقرأ وفي يأبى وجه آخر أن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.claim: Jabā-yajbā and qalā-yaqlā follow the qaraʾa pattern, but Sibawayh says these forms are known only from weakly transmitted usage.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.anchor: وقالوا جبى يجبى وقلى يقلى فشبهوا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.claim: The forms ʿamara-yaʿmuru and yaḥzuru follow the regular analogy; Sibawayh gives them as better-attested cases.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.anchor: وأما غير هذا فجاء على القياس مثل عمر يعمر ويعمر ويحزر ويحزر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.claim: Sibawayh cites waʿadahu-yaʿiduhu as an analogy for opening after a quiescent initial radical, but says ʿaḍaḍtu-taʿaḍḍu is not well attested.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماهذهالحروففيهفاءات)#709.anchor: وقالوا عضضت تعض فإنما يحتج بوعده

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p353/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p353/r2.speaker: لبيد بن ربيعة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p353/r2.claim: Labid's verses say that all children of a mother eventually become one, and the survivor is neither left nor immortal, illustrating mortality.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p353/r2.anchor: وقال لبيد بن ربيعة: كلُّ بَنىِ أمَّ وإن كثُروا. . . يوماً يصيرون إلى واحدِ

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p353/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p353/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p353/r4.claim: Across 87 Quranic occurrences of the root, eternity belongs only to the afterlife; references to worldly permanence express illusion or deny that humans can attain it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p353/r4.anchor: فلا خلود في القرآن إلا في الحياة الآخرة: في دار الخلود، أو في عذاب الخلد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p938/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p938/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p938/r3.claim: Every mutawātir reading is Qurʾān and may be recited in prayer; al-Jazarī collected the ten canonical readings in al-Nashr.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p938/r3.anchor: كل قراءة متواترة هي قرآن يمكن أن يقرأ بها في الصلاة وغيرها وهي القراءات العشر التي أحصاها الجزري

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p938/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p938/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p938/r4.claim: In ordinary language ḥasiba yaḥsabu is more common than ḥasiba yaḥsibu; the latter is rare, while ḥasaba yaḥsubu means to count.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p938/r4.anchor: أما حسَب يحسُب بالضم فهي بمعنى العدّ

ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r1.claim: Akh-ladahu means that wealth kept him alive, since it sustains life and protects him throughout his lifespan.
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r1.anchor: { أخلده } : أي أبقاه حيا ، إذ به قوام حياته وحفظه مدة عمره

ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says wealth lengthens a person's hopes and distant ambitions until, through heedlessness, he imagines it has made him immortal in this world.
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري : أي طول المال أمله ومناه الأماني البعيدة ، حتى أصبح لفرط غفلته وطول أمله

ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r3.claim: One report says al-Akhnas owned four thousand dinars.
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r3.anchor: قيل : وكان للأخنس أربعة آلاف دينار

ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:104:3/r4.claim: Another report says al-Akhnas owned ten thousand dinars.

ALUSI:104:3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:3/r1.claim: The clause yaḥsabu anna mālahu akhladahu may be circumstantial or a new independent clause.

ALUSI:104:3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:3/r2.claim: Akhlada and khallada mean to leave someone lasting forever or for a very long time.
ALUSI:104:3/r2.anchor: لا يتناهى أو مكثا طويلا جدا

ALUSI:104:3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:3/r3.claim: The verse uses an illustrative metaphor: wealth lengthens his hopes, so he builds, plants, and digs as if his money kept him alive.
ALUSI:104:3/r3.anchor: والكلام من باب الاستعارة التمثيلية والمرادان المال طول أمله ومناه الأماني البعيدة

ALUSI:104:3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:3/r4.claim: Naming māl explicitly rather than using a pronoun reinforces the point, while the past tense intensifies the intended meaning.
ALUSI:104:3/r4.anchor: والإظهار في مقام الإضمار لزيادة التقرير والتعبير بالماضي للمبالغة في المعنى المراد

ALUSI:104:3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:3/r5.claim: He may literally believe wealth grants immortality through arrogance and distraction from the Hereafter, or because he thinks life and health depend on visible causes and wealth.
ALUSI:104:3/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يراد أنه حاسب ذلك حقيقة لفرط غروره واشتغاله بالجمع والتكاثر عما أمامه من قوارع الآخرة

ALUSI:104:3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:3/r6.claim: A remote interpretation says the verse alludes to an actually immortalizing pursuit: working for the Hereafter; al-Ālūsī regards this as very far-fetched.
ALUSI:104:3/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد انه يحسب المال من المخلدات ولا نظر فيه إلى أن الخلود دنيوي

ALUSI:104:3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:3/r7.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:104:3/r7.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn suggests the miser is the subject of akhlada and wealth its object, meaning he thinks he can preserve his wealth forever; al-Ālūsī dismisses the analysis.
ALUSI:104:3/r7.anchor: وزعم عصام الدين أنه يحتمل أن يكون فاعل أخلد الحاسب ومفعوله المال أن يظن أن يحفظ ماله أبدا

BAGHAWI:104:3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:104:3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:104:3/r1.claim: He thinks his wealth has made him immortal in this world, imagining that his riches mean he will not die.
BAGHAWI:104:3/r1.anchor: يظن أنه لا يموت مع يساره

BAYDAWI:104:3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:104:3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:104:3/r1.claim: He thinks his money has left him immortal in this world, and loves it as he would love immortality.
BAYDAWI:104:3/r1.anchor: { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } تركه خالدا في الدنيا

BAYDAWI:104:3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:104:3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:104:3/r2.claim: Alternatively, love of wealth has distracted him from death.
BAYDAWI:104:3/r2.anchor: أو حب المال أغفله عن الموت

BAYDAWI:104:3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:104:3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:104:3/r3.claim: Alternatively, his long hopes made him expect immortality and act as though death would not come.
BAYDAWI:104:3/r3.anchor: أو طول أمله حتى حسب أنه مخلد

BAYDAWI:104:3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:104:3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:104:3/r4.claim: The verse alludes to striving for the afterlife as the path to lasting life.
BAYDAWI:104:3/r4.anchor: وفيه تعريض بأن المخلد هو السعي للآخرة

BIQAI:104:3/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:104:3/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:104:3/r1.claim: The clause may be read as a resumption.
BIQAI:104:3/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استئنافاً ،   وفيه تعريض

BIQAI:104:3/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:104:3/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:104:3/r2.claim: Because his intellect is deficient, he thinks his counted wealth grants him worldly immortality and loves it as he loves eternal life.
BIQAI:104:3/r2.anchor: لقلة عقله { أن ماله } أي ذلك الذي عدده

BIQAI:104:3/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:104:3/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:104:3/r3.claim: Alternatively, this is a metonym for living as if death will never come: he immerses himself in sin, turns from God, and pursues fleeting pleasures.
BIQAI:104:3/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك كناية عن أنه عمل

BIQAI:104:3/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:104:3/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:104:3/r4.claim: The verse alludes to lasting life being gained only through righteous deeds that bring felicity in the afterlife.
BIQAI:104:3/r4.anchor: وفيه تعريض بأنه لا يفيد الخلد إلا الأعمال الصالحة المسعدة في الدار الآخرة

IBNASHUR:104:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:3/r1.claim: The clause may be a circumstantial clause describing the slanderer, used to mock his greed: nobody really thinks wealth makes him immortal, so the image is a representation or an emphatic simile.
IBNASHUR:104:3/r1.anchor: وجملة :  { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } يجوز أن تكون حالاً من هُمَزة فيكون مستعملاً في التَّهكم عليه

IBNASHUR:104:3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:3/r2.claim: Alternatively, the sentence is independent and declarative for denial, or an omitted interrogative is understood, producing mockery or amazement.
IBNASHUR:104:3/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الجملة مستأنفة والخبر مستعملاً في الإِنكار ، أو على تقدير همزة استفهام محذوفة مستعملاً في التهكم أو التعجيب .

IBNASHUR:104:3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:3/r3.claim: The past tense presents a future as already accomplished because the man is certain of it, intensifying the mockery as though his wealth had already secured immortality.
IBNASHUR:104:3/r3.anchor: وجيء بصيغة المضي في { أخلده } لتنزيل المستقبل منزلة الماضي لتحققه عنده ، وذلك زيادة في التهكم به

IBNASHUR:104:3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:3/r4.claim: The hamza in أخلده is causative: his wealth supposedly made him immortal.
IBNASHUR:104:3/r4.anchor: والهَمزة في { أخلده } للتعدية ، أي جعله خالداً .

IBNASHUR:104:3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:3/r5.claim: Most reciters read yaḥsibu with kasra on the sīn; Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and Abū Jaʿfar read it with fatḥa; both are dialect forms.
IBNASHUR:104:3/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { يحسِب } بكسر السين . وقرأه ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة وأبو جعفر بفتح السين وهما لغتان .

IBNASHUR:104:3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:3/r6.claim: The hoarders resemble people who imagine wealth shields them from death and makes them immortal; earthly survival is their highest wish because they do not believe in another eternal life.
IBNASHUR:104:3/r6.anchor: ومعنى الآية : أن الذين جمعوا المال يشبه حالهم حال من يحسب أن المال يقيهم الموت ويجعلهم خالدين

IBNATIYYA:104:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:104:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:104:3/r1.claim: He imagines wealth is the substance and support of life: it preserved him through his lifetime and will keep preserving him.
IBNATIYYA:104:3/r1.anchor: وقوله : { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } معناه : يحسب أن ماله هو معنى حياته وقوامها

KASHSHAF:104:3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:104:3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:104:3/r1.claim: Akhladahu and khalladahu have the same sense: wealth lengthened his hopes and filled him with distant wishes until he imagined he would never die.
KASHSHAF:104:3/r1.anchor: { أَخْلَدَهُ } وخلده بمعنى ، أي : طوّل المال أمله ، ومنّاه الأماني البعيدة

KASHSHAF:104:3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:104:3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:104:3/r2.claim: He may build fortified structures, plant trees, and develop land as though he believes his wealth has kept him alive.
KASHSHAF:104:3/r2.anchor: أو يعمل من تشييد البنيان الموثق بالصخر والآجر وغرس الأشجار وعمارة الأرض عمل من يظن أن ماله أبقاه حيا

KASHSHAF:104:3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:104:3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:104:3/r3.claim: The wording may allude to righteous deeds, which alone make their doer abide in bliss; wealth has made no one immortal there.
KASHSHAF:104:3/r3.anchor: أو هو تعريض بالعمل الصالح ، وأنه هو الذي أخلد صاحبه في النعيم ؛ فأما المال فما أخلد أحداً فيه

KASHSHAF:104:3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:104:3/r4.speaker: unspecified report
KASHSHAF:104:3/r4.claim: A report says al-Akhnas had four thousand dinars; another gives his wealth as ten thousand.
KASHSHAF:104:3/r4.anchor: وروي أنه كان للأخنس أربعة آلاف دينار . وقيل : عشرة آلاف

KASHSHAF:104:3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:104:3/r5.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF:104:3/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan visited a wealthy man who said he had saved thousands against hard times, harsh rulers, calamities, and fear of poverty; al-Ḥasan replied that he was leaving it to people who would neither thank nor excuse him.

KASHSHAF:104:3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:104:3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:104:3/r6.claim: Kallā rebukes the miser’s assumption that wealth makes him immortal.

MAWARDI:104:3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:104:3/r1.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI:104:3/r1.claim: ʿIkrima says he imagines his wealth will increase his lifespan.
MAWARDI:104:3/r1.anchor: أحدهما : يزيد في عمره ،   قال عكرمة .

MAWARDI:104:3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:104:3/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:104:3/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says he imagines his wealth will keep him from dying.
MAWARDI:104:3/r2.anchor: الثاني : يمنعه من الموت ،   قال السدي .

MAWARDI:104:3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:104:3/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:104:3/r3.claim: A third possibility is that he thinks his wealth will benefit him after death.

NASAFI:104:3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:104:3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:104:3/r1.claim: He thinks his wealth has made him immortal in this world, so that he will not die.
NASAFI:104:3/r1.anchor: أي تركه خالداً في الدنيا لا يموت

NASAFI:104:3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:104:3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:104:3/r2.claim: Alternatively, this is an allusion to righteous deeds as what make their doer everlasting in bliss; wealth has made no one immortal.
NASAFI:104:3/r2.anchor: أو هو تعريض بالعمل الصالح ،   وأنه هو الذي أخلد صاحبه في النعيم ،   فأما المال فما أخلد أحداً فيه .

QURTUBI:104:3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:104:3/r1.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI:104:3/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the person thinks his wealth will keep him alive so he never dies.
QURTUBI:104:3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى :  " يحسب "  أي يظن { أن ماله أخلده } أي يبقيه حيا لا يموت ،   قاله السدي .

QURTUBI:104:3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:104:3/r2.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI:104:3/r2.claim: Ikrima interprets the claim as meaning that wealth will increase the person’s lifespan.
QURTUBI:104:3/r2.anchor: وقال عكرمة : أي يزيد في عمره .

QURTUBI:104:3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:104:3/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:104:3/r3.claim: Another explanation takes the verb to mean that wealth gave him life in the past, using a past form for the future.
QURTUBI:104:3/r3.anchor: وقيل : أحياه فيما مضى ،   وهو ماض بمعنى المستقبل .

QURTUBI:104:3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:104:3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:104:3/r4.claim: Arabic may say someone “perished and entered the Fire” while meaning that he will enter it, illustrating past tense used for the future.
QURTUBI:104:3/r4.anchor: يقال : هلك والله فلان ودخل النار ،   أي يدخل .

TAB:104:3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:104:3/r1.speaker: author
TAB:104:3/r1.claim: He imagines the wealth he amassed, counted, and withheld will keep him alive in this world by removing death from him.
TAB:104:3/r1.anchor: يقول : يحسب أن ماله الذي جمعه وأحصاه ، وبخل بإنفاقه ، مُخلدُه في الدنيا ، فمزيلٌ عنه الموت .

TAB:104:3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:104:3/r2.speaker: author
TAB:104:3/r2.claim: Although the verb is past in form, al-Ṭabarī reads its sense as future, “will make him immortal”; Arabic can describe a coming consequence as already accomplished, as in saying someone has perished or entered Hell before it happens.
TAB:104:3/r2.anchor: وقيل : أخلده ، والمعنى : يخلده ، كما يقال للرجل الذي يأتي الأمر الذي يكون سببا لهلاكه : عَطِب والله فلان ، وهلك والله فلان ، بمعنى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r1.claim: In comparison, the speaker focuses on the quality shared by two things and disregards their other differences.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r1.anchor: أن المشبه الشيء بالشيء من شأنه أن ينظر إلى الوصف الذي به يجمع بين الشيئين وينفي عن نفسه الفكر فيما سواه جملة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r2.claim: Calling Zayd like a lion gives him a measured share of bravery; calling him the lion makes a maximal claim, either nearly true or hyperbolic.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r2.anchor: فإن هو قال زيد كالأسد كان قد أثبت له حظا ظاهرا في الشجاعة ولم يخرج عن الاقتصاد وإذ قال هو الأسد تناهى في الدعوى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r3.claim: The lion's name is grounded chiefly in courage; its other features and qualities are secondary to that defining attribute.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r3.anchor: وأن ماعداها من صورته وسائر صفاته عيال عليها وتبع لها في استحقاقه هذا الاسم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r4.claim: One use of “he is” identifies one person known by either of two names.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r4.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون للشيء اسمان يعرفه المخاطب بأحدهما دون الآخر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r5.claim: A second use of “he is” asserts complete likeness and denies any difference or disparity between two things.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r5.anchor: والثاني أن يراد تحقيق التشابه بين الشيئين وتكميله لهما ونفي الاختلاف والتفاوت عنهما

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r6.claim: The complete-likeness sense derives from identity: two fully similar things can make a viewer at different times think he has seen the same thing.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r6.anchor: وذلك أن المتشابهين التشابه التام لما كان يحسب أحدهما الآخر ويتوهم الرائي لهما في حالين أنه رأى شيئا واحدا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r7.claim: Applied to the lion comparison, focusing only on courage and denying any difference between the two forms the hyperbolic sense of calling the person “himself.”
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p218/r7.anchor: ثم لم يثبت بين شجاعة صاحبه وشجاعة الأسد فرقا فقد صار إلى معنى قولنا وهو بلا شبهه
